summary: This work demonstrates state preparation and measurement (SPAM) errors below $10^{-3}$ for single-mode grid-state qubits in a superconducting cavity coupled to a transmon auxiliary qubit, achieving two orders-of-magnitude improvement over prior art. The improvement combines postselected stabilization-based state preparation with repeated finite-energy measurements, both fully compatible with autonomous quantum error correction.
motivation: SPAM errors have been a significant bottleneck limiting computational performance in bosonic grid-state platforms, despite their hardware-efficient approach to fault-tolerant quantum computing. Reducing SPAM errors to transmon-qubit levels ($\sim 10^{-3}$) is essential for practical bosonic architectures.
method: State preparation uses repeat-until-success compatible postselected stabilization cycles starting from vacuum or 9 dB-squeezed states, targeting six cardinal states with envelope parameter $\Delta = 0.38$ and average photon number $\bar{n}_s \approx 2.96$. Measurement employs repeated finite-energy measurements ($N_{\mathrm{RFE}} = 5$–$8$ rounds) with all-agree postselection, which suppresses auxiliary qubit readout errors (fidelity $\mathcal{V} = 0.95(1)$) and photon-loss effects. The storage mode has $T_{1,s} = 360(10)$ µs and $T_{2,s} = 640(40)$ µs; dispersive coupling $2\chi_{sq}/2\pi = -45.44$ kHz.
result: Combined SPAM error reaches $7(7) \times 10^{-4}$ with $24\%$ state-preparation and $39\%$ measurement survival probabilities. Magic-state preparation achieves $8(5) \times 10^{-3}$ SPAM error. Autonomous QEC maintains logical error per round at $\epsilon_{\mathrm{QEC}} = 0.0081(2)$, with initial logical fidelity $F_L(0)$ substantially improved without degrading QEC performance.
